newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI resumes dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI resumes dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee moved by three to four paise against the forward dollar on Tuesday on bouts of profit-booking and exporter sales, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 3.29 percent compared to the previous close of 3.23 percent.
Forward premiums opened a shade lower on Tuesday but rose on profit taking before fresh exporter sales stabilised the rates, dealers said. December and January dollars were in demand.
Exporters were selling far forwards to better their premiums, some selling June 1998 maturity, dealers said.
The spot rupee was relatively calm, closing the day unchanged at 35.81/82 against the dollar. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) resumed dollar purchases at 35.8175, dealers said.
The spot rupee was stuck at 35.81/82 throughout the day.
The foreign bank was a major seller of dollars from foreign institutional investors (FIIs) on Tuesday, dealers said.
FIIs bought 410 million rupees worth of shares and sold shares for 80 million rupees on June 27, according to latest data released by the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
